## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the loop that plays a case (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail and model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

----
# Codacabana: Tacto Negotiation Arena

Team Codacabana at the European Hackathon League Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 October 2026,
Tacto track. Our AI buyer for Hollerau Pumpenwerke negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's supplier
bots and closes the deal with the lowest total cost, or walks away. Brief: `docs/challenge.md`.

## Setup

Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
git config core.hooksPath .githooks   # secret scan, no pushes to main, Entire hooks
uv sync                               # the agent, Tacto's arena kit, pytest, ruff
cp .env.example .env                  # fill in the keys below
uv run arena data                     # data package into data/package
uv run arena me                       # the key works: team and practice quota
```

Environment variables (`.env.example`):

| Variable | What |
|---|---|
| `ARENA_URL` | `https://arena.tacto.ai` |
| `ARENA_API_KEY` | the team key from https://arena.tacto.ai/apply |
| `ARENA_DATA` | `data/package` |
| `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY` | the model, any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint; optional `LLM_EFFORT` |

## Run

```sh
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                     # one sandbox case (free)
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10     # every hosted practice case (counts against the quota)
uv run buyer pull --set practice                  # finished sessions with trace -> logs/sessions/
uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v     # the Live Final: start before 12:00, leave it running
```

## Approach

Code owns every number: `buyer/policy.py` plans terms and prices with `total_cost`, cites data
by ID and refuses bad accepts; the model writes one paragraph of each e-mail (`buyer/llm.py`).
`buyer/runner.py` plays the cases. Design in `docs/design.md`, findings in `docs/learnings.md`.

## Develop

Rules for people and coding agents: `AGENTS.md`.

```sh
uv run pytest -q                 # our agent end to end against the local arena simulator
uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format .
```
----
# docs

Ours:

- `learnings.md`: what we know about the arena, its suppliers and the data package, with evidence.
- `design.md`: the agent we are building. `how-it-works.pdf` holds its architecture diagram.
- `generalisation.md`: how well the agent should carry over to the Live Final's unseen suppliers and case types.
- `negotiation-research.md`: negotiation strategies from the literature, checked against our traces, with an experiment plan.

Tacto's, copied from [tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit](https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit)
`brief/` at commit `1b5516b` (CC BY 4.0). Upstream is the source of truth.

- `challenge.md`: the participant brief (story, task, score, rules, timeline)
- `api.md`: the HTTP API, message format, claim checks, the cost function C
- `submission.md`: what to hand in on ehl.gg by Sunday 12:00, and the pitch
----
# Copy to .env (never commit it). Real environment variables win over this file.
ARENA_URL=https://arena.tacto.ai
# The team key from https://arena.tacto.ai/apply. One per team; never commit, log or post it.
ARENA_API_KEY=
# The unpacked data package (`uv run arena data` puts it here, plus the Sunday release next to it)
ARENA_DATA=data/package

# The model: any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It has to answer well inside 60 seconds.
LLM_PROVIDER=openai
LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
LLM_MODEL=gpt-6-luna
LLM_API_KEY=

# Submission and pitch

What to hand in for the Tacto track, and how the pitch works. Deadline: **Sunday 12:00 on ehl.gg**.

## What to submit

1. **Your repo:** the agent and a README that says how to run it (setup, the environment variables it
   needs, without values, and the command). Put the **commit hash** your agent runs in the final into
   the description. The jury and tum.ai must be able to open the repo; tum.ai runs a code agent over
   every submission.
2. **A short description** of your approach: how your agent prepares, what it reads in the data, how
   it decides what to offer, and when it closes or walks away.
3. **Slides** for the pitch. The top 10 present them from 13:00.

Keep every key out of the repo: no `.env`, no LLM key, no arena key.

## At 12:00 your agent is already running

The code freeze and the Live Final start together, so start your agent before 12:00 and leave it
running:

```bash
uv run arena run --set final --agent llm --parallel 10
```

Or your own runner that polls `GET /v1/cases?set=final`. The kit's runner waits for wave 1, plays each
wave's cases in parallel within the 8-minute cap and stops after the fifth wave. From 12:00 there is no
human in the loop, and your agent must not read `/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard` or `/results`.
We check the top 10 for pushes after the freeze.

Checklist for 11:30:

- The machine and network you use for the final; one practice case went through it at the 09:00
  pre-flight.
- `uv run arena data` ran after 08:00, so the Sunday release sits next to the package.
- `uv run arena me` answers with your team: the key works.
- LLM credits and rate limits for about an hour of parallel play.
- The runner is started and logs to a file; the laptop is on power and does not sleep.

## The pitch

- **The top 10:** the ten teams with the most points after the five waves.
- **5 minutes pitch + 2 minutes of questions**, from 13:00. tum.ai keeps the time; the slot does not
  stretch.
- **Every replay is open to the jury.** After the final, each case on https://arena.tacto.ai/results
  links to its replay. Pick one negotiation and walk us through it.
- Questions to expect: Why did your agent write that? Would it have worked on a real supplier? What
  did your agent learn about suppliers, and from where?
- ⟦Q2: how the Live Final score and the jury combine for places 1-3, and the jury criteria⟧
----
   1 # Agent design
   2 
   3 The target architecture of our buyer, merged from the team's planning notes (PRs #7 to #10,
   4 10 Oct). What we learned in play is in `learnings.md`; this file says what we build.
   5 
   6 **Status.** The branch `steffen/price-engine` plays a code-only policy with a model-written
   7 paragraph (`buyer/policy.py`, run by `buyer/runner.py`): practice mean of best scores 0.73 (from
   8 0.32), sandbox D01 0.99, D02 0.73. What it does is under "Implemented" below; the rest of this file
   9 is the target design. Julian's draft two (`origin/julian/draft-two`) holds a richer stance and
  10 reader design that is not merged. The architecture diagram is on page 1 of
  11 [how-it-works.pdf](how-it-works.pdf).
  12 
  13 ## Implemented (price engine)
  14

  83 
  84 `arena_kit.cost.supplier_value` prices a deal for the supplier from `standard`, `interest_rate`,
  85 `ppm` and `extra`; `relationship_cost` needs `full_cost` and is 0 without it. So we estimate:
  86 
  87 - **Full cost**: cost-breakdown XLSX, else `should_cost` moved by its drivers' index change, else
  88   quote minus an assumed margin. A relationship charge in a practice result reveals the true margin.
  89 - **Cost of money**: cash discounts, cash-need notes, credit index, equity ratio. Seen rates: 0 to
  90   17 %/yr (`learnings.md`).

  92   evidence. Volume, contract length and index clauses are not cash in `supplier_value`.
  93 
  94 C_best estimate: the cheapest allowed sheet whose supplier value stays above its floor, or C_alt.
  95

  97 
  98 A stance per supplier (opening gap, capture, margin, justified share, steps) proposed by the model
  99 at case open, clamped by code to a range per tier and goal, logged with a reason. Fallback

 101 
 102 | Constant | Values |
 103 |---|---|
 104 | capture (share of possible saving before accepting) | leverage 0.75, quality_first 0.65, stabilise 0.6, secure_supply 0.55, routine 0.5 |

 118 3. Supplier estimate: full cost and cost of money, giving target and walk-away.

 120 5. Persona reading and pacing.
 121 6. Tune on practice traces, one change per batch.
 122

 124 
 125 - Branch on features (goal, must-haves, credit, cash signals, owner type, quote content), never on
 126   case or supplier IDs. No constants copied from one case.
 127 - Hold out two or three practice cases for checking only.
 128 - Test failure paths: late model call, malformed reply, a supplier that refuses everything,
 129   missing quote fields, a quote PDF without a standard-terms section.
 130 - Change the agent only for a lesson seen in two cases or clearly general. Freeze early.
 131

 133 
 134 Use: data-backed anchors, requests framed as trades, two or three packages to watch the choice,
 135 shrinking concessions with an ask in return, real rival offers cited by ID, a recap of every field
 136 before closing.
 137

 139 effect, `learnings.md`), squeezing a weak supplier in `stabilise` / `secure_supply`, leaking

 141 attack on the arena: never.

1 # Generalisation to the Live Final
   2 
   3 How well the agent on `steffen/price-engine` (commit `9182604`) should carry over to Sunday: new
   4 suppliers, up to a third of cases mixing supplier and case types practice never showed, some
   5 citing the 08:00 release. Research on Saturday 10 October, evening: the kit's code, all 21 case
   6 files, `logs/runs/`, `exports/`, the data package, and our agent on `arena-sim`. No practice
   7 quota spent. Same conventions as `learnings.md`: date, tag, finding, evidence, consequence.
   8 
   9 ## Verdict
  10 
  11 The code runs on every case structure we know. Its tuning is in-sample and unmeasured beyond
  12 the ten hosted cases. The biggest gaps for Sunday: new suppliers get a neutral profile because
  13 the release's letters and news never reach the persona code; one exception loses a whole case
  14 (or every later wave); four or more bidders time out.
  15 
  16 | # | Risk | Damage | Fix | Effort |
  17 |---|---|---|---|---|
  18 | 1 | an exception in a move or the wave poll | a case at its alternative (0 in 6 of 21), or all later waves | catch per move, keep polling | small |
  19 | 2 | release rows invisible to SQL; most suppliers without text | neutral profile for new suppliers | read release rows via the ID index; scan the supplier's e-mails | small to medium |

content.content:
"""The negotiation policy, per supplier thread: plan the non-price terms by C at the supplier's
own valuation, open below its quote, then move toward its counter round by round so it keeps
conceding, with verified claims spread over the rounds. Close on its final offer, its agreement or
the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.

What the suppliers showed (sandbox and practice, `docs/learnings.md`):
- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they
  would make, so our sheet stays below their counter until the end;
- every verified claim they take into account lowers where they stop, most of it in round 1;
- patience runs out at a cumulative gap of about 40 % between our sheets and their counters
  (summed per round, relative to their price), much earlier for a supplier selling near its cost
  or one that is fully booked: a final offer, or a walk-away;
- a large first concession means a deep floor: then we hold low instead of meeting it."""

import base64
import functools
import logging
import time

from arena_kit.docs import standard_terms
from arena_kit.play import latest, moves_left, standing

from . import economics as eco
from . import llm, reader, writer
from .claims import ClaimBank, rival_offer
from .personas import profile, signals_in

log = logging.getLogger("buyer")

FRACTION = 0.3  # share of the gap to the supplier's counter we move per round
# Opening price as a share of its quote at our terms, by category goal. Practice C_best sat 12 to
# 22 % below the quote in leverage, routine and secure-supply cases, 1.5 to 3 % in stabilise ones.
ANCHOR = {"leverage": 0.78, "routine": 0.82, "secure_supply": 0.88, "quality_first": 0.88, "stabilise": 0.92}
ANCHOR_MIN = 0.75  # never open lower than this share (an insult costs patience)
BUDGET = 1.0  # patience: the cumulative relative gap we show (no cap for a typical supplier)
DEEP = 0.06  # a first concession this large (share of its quote) means a deep floor
MIN_MOVE = 0.002  # every sheet moves at least this share of the price
FIRST_CLAIMS, LATER_CLAIMS = 3, 1
DONE = {"agreed", "final_offer"}
ENDED = {"walked_away", "no_bid"}


class Side:
    """One supplier thread: what we know and what we did."""

    def __init__(self, sid):
        self.sid = sid
        self.std = {}
        self.prof = {}
        self.est = {}
        self.terms = {}  # our planned non-price terms (with a price placeholder)
        self.quote = None  # its opening price at our terms
        self.last_sheet = {}  # its previous standing terms
        self.late = 0  # our messages the arena counted as rounds although they came too late
        self.anchor = None
        self.target = None  # relationship goals: the price with the lowest C
        self.budget = BUDGET
        self.claims = []
        self.ours = []  # our prices at s.terms, one per message with a sheet
        self.theirs = []  # its price at our terms, one per reply
        self.gaps = []  # relative gap of each of our sheets to its counter
        self.state = "open"  # open | mirror | closing | done | ended
        self.prev_state = "open"  # the state before the message in flight
        self.pending = None  # the message in flight: what to undo if it times out
        self.tried = set()  # (field, value) we switched away from
        self.term_change = False  # its last counter changed our non-price terms
        self.last_reply = None
        self.asks = []  # what its last e-mail asked of us (reader.asks)
        self.attached = set()  # files we already sent it


class Negotiator:
    def __init__(self, case, pkg=None, complete=None):
        self.case, self.pkg, self.complete = case, pkg, complete
        self.bank = ClaimBank(pkg, case)
        self.sides = {}
        self.used = set()  # claim IDs cited in this case (a rival quote: per supplier)
        self.notes = []  # what we decided, for the log
        self.writer_s = llm.TIMEOUT_S  # wall clock the model may take on the move being built

    # -- setup -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def setup(self, sid, events):
        case, s = self.case, Side(sid)
        s.std = safe(lambda: standard_terms(events), {}) or {}
        sheet_id, quote = standing(events)
        s.prof = safe(lambda: profile(self.pkg, sid), profile(None, sid))
        self.read_signals(s, latest(events).get("body"))
        self.sides[sid] = s
        if not sheet_id or quote.get("unit_price") is None:
            s.state = "ended"
            return s
        s.last_sheet = quote
        # a bundle's should-cost is unknown: one component's cost is not the price unit of the kit
        parts = case.get("parts") or []
        full_cost, own_plant = (
            safe(lambda: self.full_cost(parts[0], sid), (None, False)) if len(parts) == 1 else (None, False)
        )
        lead = quote.get("lead_time_days") or s.std.get("lead_time_days")
        overtime = 0.005 if "capacity_full" in s.prof["signals"] else 0.001
        s.est = eco.estimate(
            case, s.std or quote, s.prof["rate"], full_cost, safe(lambda: self.real_ppm(sid)), lead, overtime
        )
        q_price = quote["unit_price"]
        goal, signals = case["buyer"].get("category_goal"), s.prof["signals"]
        sustainable = case["buyer"].get("sustainable_margin_pct") or 0
        if full_cost and goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            # it quoted with its margin: a should-cost above that is our estimate's error (P02: 374.95
            # against a quote of 370.96; the relationship charge of the deals says about 368)
            full_cost = min(full_cost, eco.value(case, quote, s.est) * (1 - sustainable / 100))
            s.est["full_cost"] = full_cost
        ratio = ANCHOR.get(goal, 0.85)
        near_cost = bool(own_plant and full_cost >= 0.98 * q_price)  # it sells at our cost estimate
        if goal in eco.RELATIONSHIP_GOALS:
            s.budget = 0.3
        if "price_frozen" in signals:
            ratio = max(ratio, 0.95)  # its list price does not move far; a deep cut only costs patience
        if "capacity_full" in signals:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.93), min(s.budget, 0.16)
        if near_cost:
            ratio, s.budget = max(ratio, 0.97), min(s.budget, 0.14)
        current = case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        if case.get("type") == "price_increase" and current:
            ratio = min(ratio, current / q_price)  # a price increase opens at today's price at most
        ratio = max(ANCHOR_MIN, ratio)
        # terms planned at the price we open with: coverage pays off at a low price, not at the quote
        planned = safe(lambda: eco.plan_terms(case, s.std, s.est, quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.terms = planned[0] if planned else eco.complete_offer(case, eco.at_price(case, quote, q_price * ratio))
        s.anchor = s.terms["unit_price"]
        s.quote = safe(
            lambda: round(eco.price_for_value(case, s.terms, s.est, eco.value(case, quote, s.est)), 2), q_price
        )
        if full_cost and not near_cost:
            s.target = safe(lambda: eco.relationship_optimum(case, s.terms, s.std, s.est, full_cost * 0.85, s.quote))
        safe(lambda: self.trade_clause(s, quote, full_cost))
        s.claims = safe(lambda: self.bank.for_supplier(sid, q_price), [])
        self.note(
            sid,
            "setup",
            quote=quote,
            std=s.std,

the round limit; in relationship goals stop at the price where C is lowest.

- they concede only after a move from us and agree as soon as our sheet reaches the counter they

        without margin. A generic estimate (a German cost base) says little about one supplier."""

        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")

        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)

            new = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}

    def real_ppm(self, sid):
        """The defect rate it really delivers (latest scorecard), what a chargeback costs it."""
        ids = self.bank.ids(f"sc:{sid.split(':')[-1]}@")
        f = self.bank.fact(ids[-1]) if ids else None
        return f.get("ppm") if f else None

    def restore(self, sid, events):
        """A resumed session (a crash, a restart): rebuild what we sent and what it answered from
        the thread, so the next move continues the path instead of opening at the anchor again."""
        s = self.sides[sid]
        ours = [m for m in events if m.get("from") == "buyer" and m.get("term_sheets")]
        if s.state == "ended" or not ours:
            return
        s.terms = eco.complete_offer(self.case, ours[-1]["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
        theirs = None
        for m in events:
            if m.get("from") == "buyer":
                self.used.update(m.get("refs") or [])
                if m.get("term_sheets"):
                    price = self.their_price(s, m["term_sheets"][0]["terms"])
                    s.ours.append(price)
                    s.gaps.append(max(0.0, (theirs - price) / theirs) if theirs else 0.0)
            else:
                sheets = m.get("term_sheets") or []
                if sheets and sheets[0].get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None:
                    theirs = self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"])
                    if s.ours:
                        s.theirs.append(theirs)
        if events and events[-1].get("from") != "buyer" and s.theirs:
            s.theirs.pop()  # the latest reply is read by move() like any fresh reply
        self.note(sid, "restore", ours=s.ours, theirs=s.theirs, terms=s.terms)

    # -- reading its reply -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def read_signals(self, s, body):
        """Persona traits in its own e-mail (a supplier the package does not know, or news since):
        merged into the profile; a cash need raises what money now is worth to it."""
        new = [k for k in signals_in(body) if k not in s.prof["signals"]]
        if not new:
            return
        s.prof["signals"] = sorted(s.prof["signals"] + new)
        if "cash_need" in new:
            s.prof["rate"] = round(s.prof["rate"] + 0.05, 3)
            if s.est:
                s.est["interest_rate"] = s.prof["rate"]
        self.note(s.sid, "signals", new=new)

    def their_price(self, s, terms):
        """Its sheet as a price at our planned terms (same value to it)."""
        same = all(terms.get(k) == v for k, v in s.terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in terms)
        if same:
            return terms["unit_price"]
        v = eco.value(self.case, terms, s.est)
        return round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, s.terms, s.est, v), 2)

    def switch(self, s, new, why):
        """Plan new non-price terms; our last price moves to the same value for the supplier."""
        if s.ours:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.ours[-1]), s.est)
            s.ours[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        if s.theirs:
            v = eco.value(self.case, eco.at_price(self.case, s.terms, s.theirs[-1]), s.est)
            s.theirs[-1] = round(eco.price_for_value(self.case, new, s.est, v), 2)
        s.terms = {**new}
        self.note(s.sid, "switch_terms", why=why, terms={k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "unit_price"})

    def adopt(self, s, sheets):
        """Its reply changed some of our non-price terms (in its counter or an alternative): it told
        us what it values. Take a sheet's terms over when C at its price beats C of our plan at
        our counterpart of that price; when it insists on an index clause, take the clause that
        costs us least."""
        if not s.ours:
            return
        case = self.case
        standing_terms = sheets[0]["terms"]
        clause = standing_terms.get("index_clause")
        if "index_clause" in s.terms and s.terms["index_clause"] != clause and clause:
            # it will not sell this term at a fixed price (raw-material distributors) and refuses a
            # deadband: take its clause when its sheet, clause included, costs us less than its
            # last one (P08, P18: a longer contract came with it) and keeps every must-have; else
            # keep asking for a fixed price (P02: the copper clause alone cost 1.8 % of spend)
            new = {**s.terms, "index_clause": clause}
            c_now = eco.cost(case, standing_terms, s.std, s.est)
            c_before = eco.cost(case, s.last_sheet, s.std, s.est)
            if eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std) and c_now < c_before - 1.0:
                self.switch(s, new, "its index clause")
            else:
                self.note(s.sid, "keep_terms", why="its index clause costs us more", c_now=c_now, c_before=c_before)
        best_c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, s.terms, self.their_price(s, standing_terms)), s.std, s.est)
        for sheet in sheets:
            terms = sheet["terms"]
            changed = {k: v for k, v in terms.items() if k != "unit_price" and k in s.terms and s.terms[k] != v}
            changed.pop("index_clause", None)
            if not changed:
                continue
            new = {**s.terms, **changed}
            if not eco.must_haves_ok(case, new, s.std):
                continue
            if any((k, repr(v)) in s.tried for k, v in changed.items()):
                continue  # we were there before: no flip-flop
            c = eco.cost(case, eco.at_price(case, new, terms["unit_price"]), s.std, s.est)
            if c < best_c - max(1.0, 0.001 * best_c):
                best_c = c
                s.tried |= {(k, repr(s.terms.get(k))) for k in changed}
                self.switch(s, new, f"its sheet {changed} costs us less")

    # -- one move ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def move(self, sid, threads, writer_s=llm.TIMEOUT_S):
        """The next message to this supplier: {"message": ...}, or None when the thread is done.
        `writer_s`: what the supplier clocks leave for the model paragraph."""
        case, s, events = self.case, self.sides[sid], threads[sid]
        self.writer_s = writer_s
        s.prev_state = s.state
        last = latest(events)
        status = last.get("status")
        if s.state == "ended" or status in ENDED:
            s.state = "ended"
            return None
        sheets = [sh for sh in last.get("term_sheets") or [] if sh.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") is not None]
        if not sheets:
            s.state = "ended" if not standing(events)[0] else "done"
            return None
        s.std = standard_terms(events) or s.std
        fresh = s.last_reply is not last
        if fresh:
            terms_before = dict(s.terms)
            self.adopt(s, sheets)
            s.term_change = any(sheets[0]["terms"].get(k, v) != v for k, v in terms_before.items() if k != "unit_price")
            s.theirs.append(self.their_price(s, sheets[0]["terms"]))
            s.last_sheet = sheets[0]["terms"]
            s.last_reply = last
            s.asks = reader.asks(last.get("body"))
            self.read_signals(s, last.get("body"))
        theirs = s.theirs[-1]
        if s.state in ("mirror", "closing"):  # we sent its own sheet or our target: done
            s.state = "done"
            return None
        left = self.moves_left(s, events)
        if status in DONE or left <= 0:
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        if s.target and theirs <= s.target * 1.002:
            # relationship goal: below the target a lower price costs more than it saves
            s.state = "closing"
            return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, max(s.target, theirs))], [], events, theirs)
        if s.ours and theirs <= s.ours[-1]:  # it came below what we offered: take it
            return self.finish(s, sheets, events, theirs, left)
        price, n_claims = self.next_price(s, theirs)
        claims = self.pick(s, n_claims, threads)
        return self.send(s, [eco.at_price(case, s.terms, price)], claims, events, theirs)

    def moves_left(self, s, events):
        """Messages we may still send: the arena counts a late message as a round too."""
        return moves_left(self.case, events) - s.late

    def next_price(self, s, theirs):
        """Our next price at s.terms: open at the anchor; then a share of the gap, held low after a
        large concession, and within the patience budget."""
        if not s.ours:
            return s.anchor, FIRST_CLAIMS
        last = s.ours[-1]
        gap = (theirs - last) / theirs
        conceded = (s.theirs[-2] - theirs) / s.theirs[-2] if len(s.theirs) > 1 else 0.0
        share = FRACTION
        if len(s.ours) == 1 and conceded >= DEEP and not s.term_change:
            # a deep floor: a pure price drop this large means it moves fast on its own (job shops,
            # P05, D02) and agrees at our sheet next: hold the anchor (Dralveck agreed at a held
            # 27.86, at 28.07 after an 8 % step); a drop that came with terms it added (an index
            # clause, P08, P18) is not one
            share = 0.0
        left = max(0.0, s.budget - sum(s.gaps))
        new_gap = min(gap * (1 - share), left / 2)
        if s.budget < 0.2:  # a touchy supplier: small, steady gaps
            new_gap = min(new_gap, 0.015)
        price = theirs * (1 - new_gap)
        price = max(price, last * (1 + MIN_MOVE))
        price = min(price, theirs * 0.998)
        return round(max(price, last), 2), LATER_CLAIMS

    def finish(self, s, sheets, events, theirs, left):
        """Its final word, its agreement or our last message: if one of its alternatives costs us
        less than its standing sheet, send that sheet back so it agrees to it; else done."""
        case = self.case
        std = s.std
        c_stand = eco.cost(case, sheets[0]["terms"], std, s.est)
        alts = [(eco.cost(case, sh["terms"], std, s.est), sh) for sh in sheets[1:]]
        alts = [(c, sh) for c, sh in alts if eco.must_haves_ok(case, sh["terms"], std)]
        if alts and left > 0:
            c, sh = min(alts, key=lambda r: r[0])
            if c < c_stand - 1.0:
                s.state = "mirror"
                terms = {k: v for k, v in sh["terms"].items() if k in case["negotiable"]}
                return self.send(s, [eco.complete_offer(case, terms)], [], events, theirs)
        s.state = "done"
        return None

    def pick(self, s, n, threads):
        """The next unused claims for this supplier: in an RFQ the cheapest rival offer first (a new
        offer is a new argument every round), then its own claims, strongest first."""
        out = []
        rivals = []
        for other, events in threads.items():
            if other == s.sid or latest(events).get("status") in ENDED:
                continue
            oid, t = standing(events)
            if oid and t.get("unit_price") and s.theirs:
                price = self.their_price(s, t)
                if price < s.theirs[-1]:
                    rivals.append((price, rival_offer(other, oid, t["unit_price"])))
        pool = [c for _, c in sorted(rivals, key=lambda r: r[0])[:1]] + s.claims
        for c in pool:
            key = [(s.sid, i) if c.get("rival") else i for i in c["ids"]]
            if any(k in self.used for k in key):
                continue
            out.append(c)
            if len(out) >= n:
                break
        return out

    def facts(self, s, sheets, claims, moved, statements, attachments):
        """Plain statements the model may use, true by construction; its asks come first so the
        paragraph answers them (P11 froze at 45.50 after five unanswered asks for faster payment)."""
        case, out = self.case, []

"""What the data says about a supplier before the first move: owner type, the persona traits in
its notes, letters, quote remarks and news (the package and the Sunday release alike), and from
those its cost of money. Unknown suppliers (not in the package, e.g. the sandbox) get the neutral
profile; their own e-mails are scanned for the same traits as they arrive (`signals_in`)."""

import re

# One or two fixed phrases per trait in the generated texts, widened to the word forms seen across
# the whole package (restructuring programme, lowered its rating, "nickel and alloys forward").
SIGNALS = {
    "cash_need": r"pay earlier|bank is watching|cash and the banks|within 10 days|under pressure"
    r"|restructur\w*|short-time work|lower\w* (its |their )?rating|cash is tight|we like fast payers"


def supplier_texts(pkg, sid):
    """Every text about this supplier: its letters, call and meeting notes and news, from the
    package and the Sunday release (both reach `ids` and `document`), plus its quote remarks."""
    texts = []
    for ref in pkg.ids("doc:") + pkg.ids("news:"):
        row = pkg.lookup(ref) or {}
        if row.get("supplier") != sid and row.get("supplier_id") != sid:
            continue
        try:
            texts.append(pkg.document(ref))
        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - a row without a readable file: its headline still counts
            texts.append(" ".join(str(v) for k, v in row.items() if k in ("title", "headline", "body", "subject")))
    try:
        texts += [r.get("remarks") or "" for r in pkg.query("SELECT remarks FROM quotes WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))]
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite
        pass
    return texts


def profile(pkg, sid):
    """{owner_type, country, category, signals, rate, warm}; neutral when the package does not know it."""
    out = {"owner_type": None, "country": None, "category": None, "signals": [], "rate": DEFAULT_RATE, "warm": True}
    if pkg is None or not pkg.lookup(sid):
        return out
    try:
        sup = pkg.query("SELECT country, category, skonto_days, skonto_pct FROM suppliers WHERE id = ?", (sid,))
        intel = pkg.query("SELECT owner_type, staff FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (sid,))
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - no SQLite: neutral
        return out

Nordmark's cost of money as about 0 and its full cost as about 371.7; the C-minimising price is
  then 361, where we are (0.735). Another payment term does not help: the charge does not move
  with it and the payment term costs us 0.67 % per 30 days. The record 0.847 has a structure we

- 2026-10-10 `arena` **Run tally against the stop rule** (my 24 practice runs since v8): the last
  mean gain above 0.01 came with v10 (runs 14 and 15: P08 +0.12, P18 +0.14); runs 16 to 24 since
  then brought P02 +0.065 (v11) and nothing else, +0.0065 on the mean. Team mean 0.776, rank 3.

  `practice-v13-P18-forecast.log`): the same path 5.30, 5.20, 5.10, 0.621; Werdenfels' counters do
  not depend on which verified claim stands next to the falling index. That makes ten practice
  runs in a row under 0.01 on the mean: the stop rule of the night holds.

  (P05, 36.00 to 30.0 or 30.5 on its first counter) agreed at our second sheet in every run: at a
  held anchor 27.86 (0.828) and 27.92 (0.822, `practice-v12b-P05.log`), at 28.03 to 28.07 after an
  8 % step toward it (0.806, 0.81). A 3 % deeper anchor (26.79) got a lower first counter (30.0),
  a second concession to 28.0 after the hold ("you only moved a few cents, but I want to keep our
  machines running"), then a walk-away at a cumulative gap of 39 % (`practice-v12-P05.log`,

  only; the anchor stays at 0.78, the patience budget binds job shops too.

  costs us (v11).** Nordmark agreed at once to a CU-NOTATION clause with a 5 % deadband at
  358.00 and 90 days, 4.3 % below its fixed price of 374.06 at 90 days (teammate's run
  `P02_491006cd111217a3`, score 0.670); the clause costs us only the 4 % index risk on the copper
  share (0.8 % of spend), the case's path (+5 %) sits inside the deadband. The deal scored 0.67
  and not more because 358 is below the relationship optimum: the charge was 59.7k, which puts

# Learnings

What we know about the arena, its supplier bots and the data package, and what it means for the
agent. Basis, Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions covering all 10 hosted cases and 12
suppliers, 17 sandbox sessions, the team's simulator and sandbox experiments, and the data
package. Every euro figure and what-if score below was recomputed with `arena_kit.total_cost`. Evidence: `exports/` (every session, supplier thread,
e-mail and claim; schema in `exports/README.md`) and `analysis/explore.py` (the data package).

Add findings to the matching section, newest first: date, tag, the finding, its evidence (case,
session or data ID) and what it means for the agent. Tags: `arena` seen in a session, `data` from
the data package, `rules` from `docs/api.md` or the kit's code. Untested ideas go under
Hypotheses. Correct or delete entries that turn out wrong.

## Takeaways for the agent

1. **Stay below the supplier's counter until the end; it agrees the moment our sheet reaches the
   counter it would make.** D01: our 51.25 one cent under its 51.30 was agreed at once
   (sandbox `14ea35524959126f`). Moving a share of the gap each round keeps it conceding: the
   engine took the practice mean of best scores from 0.32 to 0.73.
2. **Verified claims that it "took into account" lower where it stops, most of all in round 1.**
   D01 with the same price path: no claims 50.00, delivery record 49.60, notice 49.60, should-cost
   49.30, three claims spread over rounds 48.90 (score 0.998). Which types count differs by
   supplier (table under Arguments and claims).
3. **Words move it too.** D01, identical sheets, no claims: plain 50.00, "firm" 49.90, warm and
   acknowledging its wage costs 49.60, "What would you need from us to move further on the
   price?" 49.40 (0.987). But a question repeated every round backfires: practice suppliers
   answered "volume!" where volume is fixed and stopped moving (P05, P18 v3). Answer what it
   asked; state a fixed volume as our full demand, with the figure.
4. **Patience is a budget of about 40 % cumulative gap** (sum over rounds of our sheet's distance
   to its counter, relative to its price): final offers at 41 to 42 % (D01 linear paths), 39 %
   (P07), 42 % (P08), 36 % (P18). Suppliers selling near our should-cost or with a pricing

content.content:
meeting notes, quote remarks and news, so plain patterns classify every note (`SIGNALS` in
  `analysis/explore.py`). Holiday, ISO, contact-person, packaging and trade-fair mails are noise.

## Persona signals

Phrases from `SIGNALS` in `analysis/explore.py`; levers are hypotheses until the arena column
shows evidence.

| Trait | Phrase in the data | Lever | Seen in the arena |
|---|---|---|---|
| `price_frozen` | "no room on price", "not discounted", "price list applies to all" | payment days, logistics, contract length | no price move, every trade refused (P03, P04) |
| `cash_need` | "pay earlier", "bank is watching", "within 10 days", "short-time work" | faster payment for price | asked for faster payment (P05 Fuchsreiter, P11 Kalwisz), took the 14-day sheet (P01). Dralveck asked too; its only cash signal is a 2 % cash discount for 10 days |
| `capacity_full` | "order intake is very strong", "fully booked", "allocates volumes" | a firm 12 to 24 month commitment | overtime premium for speed (P05 Hrvelec, P10 Ravensteiner) |
| `spare_capacity` | "second shift has been on hold", "take additional parts" | volume, extra parts | "We have free capacity for your parts" (P05) |
| `stale_costing` | "not followed his material", "own spreadsheet" | the real index path since its last price | conceded 1.20 after index and notice claims (P01) |
| `open_book` | "walk us through their calculation" | ask for the cost breakdown | no breakdown sent (P04, P08, P18) |
| `hedged` | "bought their ... forward", "covered at fixed prices" | index arguments fail until the hedge ends | untested |
| `approval_2pct` | "above 2 % need the approval" | moves of 2 % or less per round | untested |
| `partnership_2022` | "kept supplying at the old price" | acknowledge 2022, partnership framing | untested |
| `reference_customer` | "important reference customer" | tone, long-term framing | untested |
| `deprioritising_us` | "reviewing small accounts", "not strategic" | bundle volume or use the alternative | untested |
| `complains_late_pay` | "invoices are overdue" | promise and keep payment terms | untested |

## Practical

- 2026-10-10 `rules` Case files of all 21 cases come free from `GET /v1/cases` (no session, no
  quota). Hosted for practice: P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18; the other nine
  exist as case files only. Our probe used 15 practice sessions.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` Our writer (`buyer/llm.py`) posts to an OpenAI-compatible chat completions
  endpoint: `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_EFFORT` (not `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
  `LLM_PROVIDER` is not read); without `LLM_MODEL` the e-mails use the template. `gpt-6-luna` answered a short call in 2.0 s and wrote three move suggestions in
  12 s. Tacto: their house agent runs on a small, cheap model, and reading the data beats a
  bigger model.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` In an RFQ every thread's 60-second clock runs while we work on another.
  A waiting thread needs a message, e.g. a short question about validity, or it collects
  timeouts; our probe kept waiting threads alive this way (D02, P05).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` `arena-sim` plays a scripted supplier: good for plumbing and timing, not
  for tactics.

## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)

- The P08 record (0.92) comes from a lower round-1 counter, not from later rounds: our later
  rounds converge to the same price whatever the gap. (P02's gap is the clause, see Agent
  experiments.)
- Three sheets of equal C for us in round 1 reveal what each lever is worth to the supplier
  (payment, lead time, ppm) and could lift P10 and P11.
- The close response of a final case carries `c_best`; calibrating anchors between waves from it
  is possible but needs a rules check first.
- Persona-specific wording beyond the generic paragraph (cash need, partnership 2022, reference
  customer) moves the round-1 counter.
- Prices fall much further when every sheet stays below the supplier's price and concessions
  are slow (house agent 0.75 on P08, ours 0.11 after agreeing in round 2).
- Cash-short suppliers give more price for 14 to 30 days payment than the 0.67 % per 30 days it
  costs us.
- Citing the best rival offer moves RFQ bidders; our probe never cited offers.
- Suppliers with "approval above 2 %" notes move at most 2 % per round.
- Stale-costing suppliers concede after a verified falling-index claim; hedged suppliers answer
  index claims with "not our reality" until the hedge ends.

meeting notes, quote remarks and news, so plain patterns classify every note (`SIGNALS` in
  `analysis/explore.py`). Holiday, ISO, contact-person, packaging and trade-fair mails are noise.

## Persona signals

Phrases from `SIGNALS` in `analysis/explore.py`; levers are hypotheses until the arena column
shows evidence.

| Trait | Phrase in the data | Lever | Seen in the arena |
|---|---|---|---|
| `price_frozen` | "no room on price", "not discounted", "price list applies to all" | payment days, logistics, contract length | no price move, every trade refused (P03, P04) |
| `cash_need` | "pay earlier", "bank is watching", "within 10 days", "short-time work" | faster payment for price | asked for faster payment (P05 Fuchsreiter, P11 Kalwisz), took the 14-day sheet (P01). Dralveck asked too; its only cash signal is a 2 % cash discount for 10 days |
| `capacity_full` | "order intake is very strong", "fully booked", "allocates volumes" | a firm 12 to 24 month commitment | overtime premium for speed (P05 Hrvelec, P10 Ravensteiner) |
| `spare_capacity` | "second shift has been on hold", "take additional parts" | volume, extra parts | "We have free capacity for your parts" (P05) |
| `stale_costing` | "not followed his material", "own spreadsheet" | the real index path since its last price | conceded 1.20 after index and notice claims (P01) |
| `open_book` | "walk us through their calculation" | ask for the cost breakdown | no breakdown sent (P04, P08, P18) |
| `hedged` | "bought their ... forward", "covered at fixed prices" | index arguments fail until the hedge ends | untested |
| `approval_2pct` | "above 2 % need the approval" | moves of 2 % or less per round | untested |
| `partnership_2022` | "kept supplying at the old price" | acknowledge 2022, partnership framing | untested |
| `reference_customer` | "important reference customer" | tone, long-term framing | untested |
| `deprioritising_us` | "reviewing small accounts", "not strategic" | bundle volume or use the alternative | untested |
| `complains_late_pay` | "invoices are overdue" | promise and keep payment terms | untested |

## Practical

- 2026-10-10 `rules` Case files of all 21 cases come free from `GET /v1/cases` (no session, no
  quota). Hosted for practice: P01, P02, P03, P04, P05, P07, P08, P10, P11, P18; the other nine
  exist as case files only. Our probe used 15 practice sessions.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` Our writer (`buyer/llm.py`) posts to an OpenAI-compatible chat completions
  endpoint: `LLM_BASE_URL`, `LLM_MODEL`, `LLM_API_KEY`, `LLM_EFFORT` (not `OPENAI_API_KEY`,
  `LLM_PROVIDER` is not read); without `LLM_MODEL` the e-mails use the template. `gpt-6-luna` answered a short call in 2.0 s and wrote three move suggestions in
  12 s. Tacto: their house agent runs on a small, cheap model, and reading the data beats a
  bigger model.
- 2026-10-10 `rules` In an RFQ every thread's 60-second clock runs while we work on another.
  A waiting thread needs a message, e.g. a short question about validity, or it collects
  timeouts; our probe kept waiting threads alive this way (D02, P05).
- 2026-10-10 `rules` `arena-sim` plays a scripted supplier: good for plumbing and timing, not
  for tactics.

## Hypotheses (untested in the arena)

- The P08 record (0.92) comes from a lower round-1 counter, not from later rounds: our later
  rounds converge to the same price whatever the gap. (P02's gap is the clause, see Agent
  experiments.)
- Three sheets of equal C for us in round 1 reveal what each lever is worth to the supplier
  (payment, lead time, ppm) and could lift P10 and P11.
- The close response of a final case carries `c_best`; calibrating anchors between waves from it
  is possible but needs a rules check first.
- Persona-specific wording beyond the generic paragraph (cash need, partnership 2022, reference
  customer) moves the round-1 counter.
- Prices fall much further when every sheet stays below the supplier's price and concessions
  are slow (house agent 0.75 on P08, ours 0.11 after agreeing in round 2).
- Cash-short suppliers give more price for 14 to 30 days payment than the 0.67 % per 30 days it
  costs us.
- Citing the best rival offer moves RFQ bidders; our probe never cited offers.
- Suppliers with "approval above 2 %" notes move at most 2 % per round.
- Stale-costing suppliers concede after a verified falling-index claim; hedged suppliers answer
  index claims with "not our reality" until the hedge ends.
- The cost floor is full cost; the five that once sold below full cost may go lower.
- A faster payment package beats a deeper price anchor for cash-short suppliers; test 20 / 30 %
  openings against standard / early payment as a 2x2, several runs per credit stratum.
- A `selective` rebuttal (naming the cost driver the supplier left out of its letter) moves more
  than a plain index claim.

# Exports: the Saturday probe sessions as tables

Every session we played on Saturday 10 October: 15 practice sessions (all 10 hosted cases) and 17
sandbox sessions, joined with the case files and the data package. What we learned from them is
in `docs/learnings.md`. Money is EUR over the case horizon; C is the arena's total cost
(`arena_kit.total_cost`), lower is better. This is a snapshot: the probe and the script that built
it (`buyer/autoprobe.py`, `analysis/export.py`) are in the closed PR #5, commit `03c51bc`.

| File | One row per | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `sessions.csv`, `.jsonl` | session | outcomes: score, C open/deal/alt/best, deal terms, cost breakdown |
| `threads.csv`, `.jsonl` | supplier in a session | supplier profile from the data next to what it did |
| `messages.jsonl` | e-mail, both directions | the full negotiation: terms with C, status, claims, reasons, back office |
| `claims.csv` | data argument we made | which arguments the arena verified, and for whom |

Join keys: `session_id` (+ `supplier_id`, + `round`). `set` is `practice` or `sandbox`.

## How we played

`method` in `sessions`:

- `autoprobe v1`: a fixed experiment per supplier thread, then the cheapest valid close. Its steps
  are `probe_step` in `messages` and `probe_steps` in `threads`:
  - `open`: questions and documents (cost breakdown, delivery schedule or 8D), our anchor price
  - `ours`: up to 3 sheets at the supplier's price, each with one lever moved our way
  - `theirs`: up to 3 sheets a step below, each with one lever moved its way
  - `claims`: up to 3 verified data arguments with a concession
  - `step`: concessions until `final_offer` or `agreed`; `push`: one ask after `agreed`
  - `keepalive`: a short question so a waiting RFQ thread does not time out
- `scripted probe (resumed by hand)`: an earlier version of the same steps (P01, first P10 run).
| `c_open`, `c_deal`, `c_alt`, `c_best` | C of the best opening quote, our deal, our alternative, the best package any supplier would accept (hidden floor, revealed after the session) |
| `gap_to_best_eur` | `c_deal - c_best`: money left on the table |
| `implied_price_at_deal_terms` | the unit price at which our deal's other terms would cost exactly `c_best`; it keeps the deal's coverage, so for an under-covered deal (P08, P18) it mixes coverage and price |
| `deal_*` | the closed terms (unstated fields filled with the supplier's standard terms) |
| `cost_*` | `c_deal` by part: price, uncovered_need, fallback_risk, payment_terms, freight, late_delivery, quality, tooling, index_clause, index_risk, relationship |

## threads

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `country`, `owner_type`, `credit_index`, `scorecard_colour`, `data_signals` | from the data package (`analysis/explore.py`, `analysis/out/profiles.csv`); signals are persona traits found in notes, letters and news, e.g. `cash_need`, `price_frozen`, `capacity_full` |

| `documents`, `sent_cost_breakdown` | attachments it sent |
| `probe_steps` | our experiment sequence (see above) |
| `questions`, `backoffice_calls` | its recurring questions; its internal decisions ("My call: counter / hold / accept") |

# Negotiation strategies: research for our buyer agent

Research report, 10 October 2026. Two inputs: (1) the literature on automated negotiation,
bargaining, procurement practice and LLM negotiators, gathered by ten parallel research agents;
(2) our own 62 logged practice sessions (`logs/sessions/`), read again to see which of those ideas
fit the arena's supplier bots. Each recommendation says what supports it and how to test it. Most
literature points were read from abstracts and summaries, not full papers: treat effect sizes as
directional (sources and confidence at the end).

## Summary

The current price engine scores a mean of **0.73** over the ten hosted cases (best run per case).
The gaps that remain are concentrated: P10 (0.68, 194k EUR from C_best), P08 (0.55, 79k), P18
(0.49, 37k), P11 (0.71, 28k), P07 (0.75, 23k), P02 (0.51, 23k).

What the traces show about the bots, in literature terms: a **behaviour-dependent conceder**
(Faratin, Sierra and Jennings' tactic family) that answers each of our steps with a smaller step
of its own, becomes a little more generous late, and ends the dance with `final_offer` once its
patience is used up. It ends the dance after 2 to 6 of our messages, so the 10-message limit
never binds. **The first counter decides most of the deal.**

Recommendations, ranked by expected gain against cost to build:

| # | Change | Why | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Make round 1 count:** three equal-C sheets (MESO), the strongest claims, a precise anchor with a reason | the first counter holds 40 to 100 % of our final price cut; MESOs anchor harder and reveal priorities | sandbox D01/D02, then P07, P08, P18 |
| 2 | **Answer the supplier's stated need every message**, also when the term is fixed | P11 Kalwisz asked for faster payment five times ("you haven't addressed this at all"), then stopped at 45.50 | P11 replay |
| 3 | **Concede in currencies, not price:** hold one or two terms it values back from round 1 and spend one per round as our move | concessions are only answered after a move; logrolling moves price without paying price | sandbox, then P07 / P08 |
| 4 | **Spend patience in fewer, larger steps** | the bot gives back only 0.2 to 0.7 of each step and stops on a cumulative gap; many small steps burn patience without buying price | sweep `FRACTION` 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 on the sandbox (free) |
| 5 | **Expected-value acceptance after `final_offer`** | pushing after `final_offer` walked once (D01); the gain from one more step is small | already behind `BUYER_PUSH_FINAL`; decide from data |

directional (sources and confidence at the end).

content.content:
Score is total cost C, not price. Every step has a fallback that still sends a move within 60 s.

## A case

1. **Prepare** (before the first move, about 20 s): open the session, build a case brief: C_open,
   C_alt, target, walk-away, the lever table (C of each allowed option), a view of each supplier,
   and a claim bank of verified arguments. (Target, not built: a stance call proposes
   per-supplier parameters and code clamps them; today the constants under Policy decide.)
2. **Negotiate**, one thread negotiator per supplier, in parallel. Each round:

   ```
   supplier reply
     -> READ    (model, hard timeout)  offer, intent, objections, statements
     -> CHECK   (code)  supplier statements against the data
     -> PLAN    (code)  candidate sheets scored with total_cost, filtered by must_haves_ok

- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for AI coding agents in this repo. Humans follow them too.

Hackathon repo, EHL Grand Finale, Munich, 10 to 11 Oct 2026. Code freeze and Live Final Sunday
12:00. Working agent first, polish second.

## Rules

- Do not preserve backward compatibility. Remove obsolete paths instead of adding layers,
  fallbacks or migrations.
- Choose the simplest implementation that fully meets the current requirement. No speculative
  abstractions, configuration or indirection.
- Grow in layers on a product that already works. Never trade a working agent for unfinished
  complexity.
- Keep components modular and concerns separated.
- Read `arena_kit` (in `.venv`) before writing a helper: cost function, quote parsing, data lookup
  and runners exist. We wrap the kit, never patch it. Guide:
  https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit/tree/main/starter-kit
- Never commit secrets. Keys live in `.env`. Never print, log or paste the arena key anywhere.
- All changes go through a PR against `main`, reviewed by one teammate. Branch `<firstname>/<topic>`.
  Agents may commit, push their branch and `gh pr create`; never push to `main`, force-push or merge.
- Run `uv run pytest -q && uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` before every PR.
- No em-dashes in prose or copy. Be terse: after an action, state what changed in three lines.

## The challenge

We are the purchasing team of Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Our agent negotiates by e-mail with Tacto's
supplier bots (LLM personas with hidden economics) and closes one term sheet per case, or walks.

- **Score** per case: `(C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best)`, clipped to 0..1. C is total cost
  over the horizon (price, uncovered need, payment, freight, lead time, quality, tooling, index
  clause, relationship charge), computed exactly by `arena_kit.total_cost`. No deal scores the
  alternative (0 if none). A broken must-have scores 0.
- **Live Final**: five waves of hidden cases, 8 minutes each, a wave's cases in parallel. Wave
  score = mean case score x 100; total = sum. New suppliers; up to a third mix supplier and case
  types practice never shows; some cite the Sunday 08:00 data release.

**Hard rules, breaking one can disqualify us:**
- No human in the loop during the final. The runner starts before 12:00 and is left alone.
- Agent code never calls `/v1/events`, `/v1/events/stream`, `/screen`, `/v1/screen`,
  `/leaderboard`, `/v1/leaderboard`, `/results`, `/v1/results`.
- One key per team. No attacks on the arena or other teams (prompt-injecting bots counts).
- The final runs the commit we submit at 12:00. No pushes after that.

**Hard limits:**
- 60 s per message per thread from the supplier's reply; three timeouts in a row end the thread.
- 10 messages per thread, up to 3 term sheets per message, every sheet carries every `negotiable`
  field.
- Max 3 claim checks per message, one per sentence, ID and figure in the same sentence. A wrong
  figure or unknown ID is `contradicted` and costs trust.
- 10 calls/s and 10 open sessions per key.
- **Practice quota: 200 sessions per rolling 24 h for the whole team.** Sandbox (`case:D01`,
  `case:D02`) and the local simulator are free.

## Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `docs/learnings.md` | **read first**: what we know about the arena, suppliers and data, with evidence |
| `docs/design.md` | the agent we are building: modules, data, policy, build order |
| `docs/challenge.md`, `api.md`, `submission.md` | Tacto's brief, API and cost formula, hand-in (upstream copies) |
| `buyer/policy.py`, `runner.py` | the price engine: per-thread policy and the supplier's asks; the loop that plays a case and the Live Final waves (`docs/design.md`, Implemented) |
| `buyer/economics.py`, `claims.py`, `personas.py`, `writer.py`, `llm.py` | C and term planning, claim bank, persona signals, e-mail composition, model paragraph |
| `buyer/cli.py` | `buyer play`, `buyer run`, `buyer pull`, `--agent naive` |
| `tests/` | end to end against `arena-sim`, no network, no model |
| `exports/` | Saturday probe sessions as CSV/JSONL; schema in `exports/README.md` |
| `analysis/explore.py` | data package exploration: profiles, persona signals, report page |
| `data/package/` | the data package (gitignored); Sunday also `data/release-sunday/` |
| `logs/sessions/<set>/` | finished sessions with trace and back office (gitignored; Saturday's committed with `-f`) |
| `logs/runs/`, `logs/practice-v*.log` | our decisions per move (anchor, terms, claims, prices) and the practice run logs |

The MCP server `arena-data` (`.mcp.json`) gives SQL, ID lookup and documents over the package.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                         # install (Python 3.12)
uv run arena data                               # data package into data/
uv run arena me                                 # key works? quota left?
uv run buyer play case:D01 -v                   # sandbox: free
uv run buyer play case:P01 -v                   # practice: costs 1 of the team's 200
uv run buyer run --set practice --parallel 10   # all hosted practice cases: costs 10
uv run buyer pull --set practice                # finished sessions -> logs/sessions/
uv run arena-sim serve --no-clock --data data/package   # local API, scripted supplier
uv run --with pandas python analysis/explore.py # data package -> analysis/out/
```

`--agent naive` plays the kit's baseline instead of ours.

## Working on the negotiation agent

- **Code owns numbers, the model owns words.** Every binding value (sheet, accept, walk away) is
  computed or checked in code with `total_cost` and `must_haves_ok`; every figure in an e-mail
  comes from code next to its data ID.
- **Never accept** a sheet that breaks a must-have or costs more than the alternative. Price
  unstated fields at the supplier's standard terms (`arena_kit.docs.standard_terms`).
- **Read the supplier.** What moves it is in the data (call notes, letters, news, quote remarks,
  payment history, scorecards). Trade what is cheap for us for what it values.
- **Score every lever per case.** The same term helps in one case and hurts in the next
  (coverage, payment days, start date, index clause, contract length).
- **Generalise.** No logic keyed on case or supplier IDs; runtime knowledge from the data package
  is fine if it works for unseen suppliers.
- **Don't leak** urgency, budget, a missing alternative or the target price.
- **Every model call has a hard timeout** well under 60 s, and the move still goes out if it
  fails. Measure latency per move.

## The learning loop

1. Try on the simulator or sandbox first. Spend practice quota only on a change you expect to
   help; check `uv run arena me` before batch runs.
2. After practice: `uv run buyer pull`, read `logs/sessions/` (trace, back office, cost breakdown).
3. Find why C_deal missed C_best, change the agent, score candidate sheets offline, play again.
4. Record each finding in `docs/learnings.md` in the same PR: date, tag (`arena` / `data` /
   `rules`), finding, evidence (session, case or data ID), consequence for the agent. Untested
   ideas go under Hypotheses; correct or delete entries that turn out wrong. Design changes go
   into `docs/design.md`. No new doc files without a reason.

## Sunday

- 08:00: `uv run arena data` again; the release lands in `data/release-sunday/`.
- 09:00: pre-flight, one practice case through the final machine and setup.
- 11:30: checklist in `docs/submission.md` (key, data, LLM credits, power, no sleep, log file).
- Before 12:00, from `main`: `uv run buyer run --set final --parallel 10 -v 2>&1 | tee logs/final.log`,
  then submit that commit hash on ehl.gg.
